idiom_name: Result<Success, Failure> with map/flatMap and a switch
implementation_notes: The standard library defines Result<Success, Failure: Error> as a frozen enum with success and failure cases, plus map/flatMap/mapError/flatMapError for chaining and init(catching:) to convert a throwing call at the boundary; get() rethrows the failure as a typed error. It is the canonical carrier when the failure must be stored, passed to a callback or delivered later (async APIs, Combine's publisher), whereas untyped throws remains the default for synchronous code. Consume it with an exhaustive switch or with mapError/flatMap chains; the failure is an Error-conforming domain enum, never a string, and force-unwrapping the success case is the trap to avoid.
pitfalls: Force-unwrapping the case (try!) reintroduces the crash and discards the error typing; use a switch or try? with a default.
The failure type must conform to Error, so domain enums need conformance even when they are never thrown.
Error type erasure returns the moment the result is turned into an untyped throws function; keep the typed failure where the caller branches.

variants.name: Typed throws throws(E) (Swift 6)
variants.implementation_notes: Swift 6 implements typed throws (SE-0413): a function can declare throws(PortError) and callers catch exhaustively without casting, and Result.get() rethrows the result's Failure type, so Result and throws interconvert losslessly. The failure then travels through the error effect (try/do-catch) rather than as a stored value, which the proposal keeps as the better default for most code and recommends where the error set is fixed and exhaustively handled - the same places a Result would otherwise be carried. Use throws(E) for synchronous APIs whose error set is closed and deliberately typed; keep Result when the failure must be held as a value or delivered asynchronously.
variants.idiom_name: func f() throws(E) -> T with exhaustive catch
pitfalls: Typed throws is a signature change: widening the error set later breaks callers that catch exhaustively, unlike the erased form.
Swift 6.0 covers synchronous typed throws (closure type inference was deferred), so async pipelines still need Result or the untyped form.
